name: gitlab
summary: GitLab's built-in MCP server on GitLab.com (projects, merge requests, work items, pipelines), browser sign-in
notes: Sign in with your GitLab account in the browser: lotr setup gitlab. GitLab registers the client itself (dynamic client registration); nothing to create first. Such a client can only get the mcp scope.
On GitLab.com the MCP server must be allowed for your top-level group (a group Owner setting). Every tool still checks your own permissions.
Self-managed or Dedicated: copy this template, set connect.url to https://YOUR-HOST/api/v4/mcp and network.hosts to YOUR-HOST.

Asks first (consent): accept_merge_request (merges), save_pipeline (creates, runs, retries, cancels pipelines), manage_pipeline (deletes pipelines), start_duo_session and send_duo_session_input (run Duo sessions in CI jobs, may use credits). Commits, branches, merge requests, notes and work items are ordinary writes.
offline_access is off: GitLab does not use that scope; it issues refresh tokens on its own.

Alternative: a fine-grained personal access token (MCP tool resource, Execute permission) as a bearer key would be the mcp-http-key archetype; legacy personal, project and group tokens are refused by the server.
